_readme: S750, the cheap piles (2026-11-28). Plan s750a files the reading state_course_not_on_page (kb/_program_named_gaps.py, S748) where the committed capture finds a state-listed course on no line of the program's own page. The reading's fires are wrong about 4 times in 100, so each row is checked against a free read of its own page before it is planned: this read prints the page so a session and the plan's second reader can see whether any line prints the course. No model call, nothing written. Palomar Apprenticeship-Carpentry A.S. 08929 and certificate 22528, one shared section: AP C 730. One load: the filed address with the data its own scripts fetch (the calls name the entry's id, which a later cq_view read needs).

questions.apc_730: Whether the Apprenticeship-Carpentry section prints AP C 730 on any line, each AP C 72x and 73x row it prints, and how its heading names the degree and the certificate.

outside_hosts.curriqunet.com: the college's own catalog (palomar.curriqunet.com), served on its catalog vendor's domain; the page's own scripts fetch the entry's text from it

46149637666.apc_730: no line of the rendered page prints AP C 730. The page is headed 'Apprenticeship-Carpentry - A.S. Degree Major/Cert. Achievement (18 units or more)', one section for the degree and the certificate, and prints 69 course codes, 58 of them AP C rows: after AP C 729 come AP WE 730, AP WE 731, AP WE 732 and AP WE 733, then AP C 735; and Total: 28.0. Of the strings the read looked for in the page's own data call (_getPage?catalogId=27&id=32956, the entry's Program Requirements), it holds 'AP C 729' and 'AP C 735' and no 'AP C 730'
46149637666._what: A session's findings over the run's log (not quoted lines): the rows the page prints, counted by a scratch script from the downloaded log and read by eye. kb/_program_piles_s750a.py cites them beside the capture's own finding.
46149637666._rows_what: For each question, the course codes of the missing course's subject that the page prints, as printed (Palomar: every course code the page prints), in page order, each once: tests/program_piles_s750a_test.py reads them against the capture's codes_found.
